subject.title: fix(reply): strip leaked current-message scaffolding and (no output) placeholders

question: Should maintainers accept the shared reply sanitizer/normalizer semantics after a rebase and exact-head validation, or require live Telegram proof first?
rationale: The patch is a focused bug fix, but it changes central suppression logic that can drop or alter user-visible replies across channels, so final message-delivery risk belongs to an owner review.

options.title: Land After Refresh
options.body: Rebase onto current main, confirm focused tests and required CI at the exact head, then land without another code change.

options.title: Request Live Channel Proof
options.body: Ask for a Mantis or contributor Telegram recording if maintainers want end-to-end visual evidence before landing.

options.title: Pause For Redesign
options.body: Pause only if owners reject central sanitizer-level suppression and want a different reply contract.

recommendation.title: Land After Refresh
recommendation.body: Rebase onto current main, confirm focused tests and required CI at the exact head, then land without another code change.

likelyOwner.reason: `vincentkoc` has recent and historical ownership signals in the shared reply-normalization boundary this PR changes.
